transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-14 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~42 minutes | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood CSM); Marta (BlueArc Head of Platform), Devon (SRE), Priya (Security), Zack (ML Eng)

Summary: quick status on creds, walked through small benchmark anomalies, validated staging access steps, listed security docs to share.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a tight 40ish minute check-in — quick round of who has anything blocking on access, then Lena will walk through the latest bench numbers, then Priya had a few security items right, P r i y a?

[00:18] Marta (BlueArc): Hi! Marta here, no blockers on my side, but we want to make sure the staging gateway creds are stable this week. we've had a couple of token expiry flukes last sprint.

[00:32] Devon (BlueArc SRE): yeah the expiry; we think it was a clock drift on the ephemeral token service but we haven't root-caused it yet.

[00:45] Samir (Redwood): ok good callout. Omar and I flagged a sticky note to re-issue long-lived staging creds so you can run baseline tests without rotation noise. Omar?

[00:55] Omar (Redwood CSM): Yep, plan is to provision staging service account creds with a 30-day TTL for the pilot harness only. we'll send the keys via secure artifact link once Priya gives a thumbs-up on the transfer method.

[01:10] Priya (BlueArc Security): my concern is the transfer and where the keys live. do you use H S M / K M S integration for keys in Redwood Private? and is there key rotation automation?

[01:28] Lena (Redwood SE): short answer: yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private; for Hosted/Dedicated we have KMS options and we recommend HSM-backed keys for regulated PHI environments. rotation can be automated on a schedule, but for the POC we can keep a manual cadence to reduce churn.

[01:45] Zack (BlueArc ML): are there any latency implications when KMS calls are in the critical path for token unwrap? because our pipeline is sensitive to sub-50ms tail.

[02:00] Lena (Redwood SE): good question. KMS unwraps are outside the token path for model inference; we cache decrypted secrets in a short-lived in-memory cache — so typical extra latency is negligible per request. the critical path for tokens is the model runtime and the kv cache behavior.

[02:18] Devon (BlueArc SRE): can you explain the KV cash — sorry, kv cache — behaviour a bit, we've seen inconsistent per-token throughput in the morning run.

[02:32] Lena (Redwood SE): sure, so Redwood's runtime keeps a per-session KV cache that holds decoded key value entries (the attention cache). when sessions re-use prefixes it avoids recomputing tokens. irregularities happen when we see lots of cold starts or resharding events. for the POC we can pin a config to keep session affinity and small batch sizes to stabilize tail latency.

[02:50] Marta (BlueArc): would pinning affect cost dramatically? we have cost goals for the pilot.

[03:02] Samir (Redwood): there's always a latency vs cost tradeoff. pinning sessions increases reserved state and might nudge cost up slightly, but it reduces tail latency spikes which seem to be your primary metric today. we can experiment with a hybrid: pin 10% of sessions for critical traffic.

[03:20] Priya (BlueArc Security): back to creds: do you log each key access? audit logs? we need proof for the compliance pack.

[03:32] Samir (Redwood): yes, audit logs are available — token-level traces in the Console, KMS access logs are forwarded, and we can provide an excerpt of the SOC2 artifact set we discussed. i'll send the SOC2 snapshot and the KMS/hsm integration note after the call.

[03:50] Priya (BlueArc Security): cool, please include retention windows and whether logs are tamper-evident.

[04:02] Samir (Redwood): noted.

[04:10] Lena (Redwood SE): ok switching to benchmarks — i uploaded the CSV to the pilot folder but i'll walk through highlights: we ran 3 runs of your prompt set with sequence lengths at 512/1024. average tokens/sec looked fine but tail p95 increased during run 2.

[04:32] Zack (BlueArc ML): is that with batching on? we try to emulate production burstiness — so small batch sizes and lots of simultaneous sessions.

[04:42] Lena (Redwood SE): yes, runs included continuous batching with a small window. the p95 jump correlates with a few reshard events on the cluster at 03:14 in the run log. i'll attach the run IDs.

[04:58] Devon (BlueArc SRE): reshard events — were those autoscaling actions or maintenance?

[05:08] Lena (Redwood SE): autoscaling; the policy triggered because a parallel experiment used burst capacity. we've put a soft quota for your pilot pool to avoid noisy neighbors.

[05:22] Marta (BlueArc): we noticed a couple of weird tokens in output sometimes — small hallucinations that bias clinical terms — any thoughts?

[05:34] Lena (Redwood SE): hallucination is probably model/regression related, not serving infra. we can pin to a model checkpoint you vetted or add prompt-level safety layers. also we can run an eval harness against your gold set to measure quality regressions.

[05:50] Zack (BlueArc ML): could we schedule a quality eval run? i can provide the gold set.

[05:56] Samir (Redwood): yes, Lena will own that with you.

[06:05] Lena (Redwood SE): i'll set up the eval run, share the harness instructions. to the earlier point on p95, immediate mitigation is to pin session affinity and reduce background reshard triggers. longer term we can recommend a quant profile that keeps quality but reduces memory pressure.

[06:25] Priya (BlueArc Security): about SSO mapping — our user mapping is SAML. does Redwood Console support SAML 2.0 for role mapping?

[06:36] Samir (Redwood): yes, Console supports SAML and OIDC. role mappings for RBAC can be configured and we can show a quick demo of the SSO flow. for Private deployments you can bring your IdP and have SCIM for provisioning.

[06:50] Priya (BlueArc Security): will need a sample assertion and the metadata to feed into our IdP.

[06:58] Omar (Redwood CSM): we'll share SAML metadata; samir will attach the SSO guide in the follow-up email.

[07:10] Devon (BlueArc SRE): network question: for staging VPC peering, what CIDR and ports need to be opened? also any recommendations for NATing egress?

[07:22] Lena (Redwood SE): we'll share a minimal network layout: peering with your staging VPC, allow egress to our control plane on 443, and open 9090 for the pilot observability endpoint. NAT depends on your policy; we support both NAT and private link style setups.

[07:40] Marta (BlueArc): can you run a quick checklist of what you need from us today to get full staging green?

[07:50] Samir (Redwood): yeah checklist time: 1) confirm staging service account creds delivery method (Priya to approve), 2) VPC peering + open ports, 3) SAML metadata for SSO, 4) provide gold test set for evals, 5) agree on pilot success criteria doc and rollback triggers.

[08:10] Priya (BlueArc Security): for creds, we prefer secrets be stored in our KMS — so rather than handing you a long-lived secret we want a short-lived token exchange. does Redwood support STS-style token exchange?

[08:24] Lena (Redwood SE): we support STS exchanges for VPC/private options; for hosted POC we can broker via a secure transfer but it's less ideal for production. for the POC we can do a one-time wrapped key transfer into your KMS and show the unwrap process.

[08:42] Devon (BlueArc SRE): can we do an on-call window during the transfer? last time a stray ip rule blocked the agent and we had to scramble.

[08:51] Omar (Redwood CSM): absolutely, we'll stand up a 1-hour provisioning window with an ops engineer on both sides.

[09:00] Samir (Redwood): ok moving on, Lena — can you walk us through the CSV highlights you mentioned?

[09:08] Lena (Redwood SE): sure; main point: average latency for seq512 was 38ms median, p95 112ms in run 1; run 2 p95 spiked to 240ms during reshard. token cost stayed within expected, but the memory pressure in run 2 indicated we had to evict some session caches which increased compute.

[09:30] Zack (BlueArc ML): 240ms p95 is high for our SLAs. is there a way to repro locally with a smaller cluster?

[09:38] Lena (Redwood SE): we can reproduce with a synthetic workload that mirrors your concurrency profile. i'll provide the seed script. we'll also provide per-run trace IDs so you can correlate to your logs.

[09:52] Marta (BlueArc): what about model variants — is there a cheaper quantized variant you recommend for staging to reduce memory without sacrificing our clinical constraints?

[10:02] Lena (Redwood SE): yes we have a quant-2 and a quant-4 profile. quant-4 reduces memory significantly with small quality delta on casual prompts; for clinical prompts we usually recommend running a quality eval first. we can stage quant-4 as a low-cost shadow to measure regressions.

[10:18] Samir (Redwood): that ties into rollback: if quant profile leads to unacceptable accuracy drop we need an automated fallback to the full-precision variant. we can set a canary that switches on error or quality regression thresholds.

[10:32] Priya (BlueArc Security): also audit: if we fall back to another model, does the audit trail capture the switch?

[10:40] Lena (Redwood SE): yes, call-level metadata includes model variant and reason codes — all surfaceable in the Console.

[10:50] Devon (BlueArc SRE): you mentioned you put a soft quota on our pilot pool to avoid noisy neighbors — can you confirm the soft quota values and whether it blocked autoscale earlier?

[11:02] Lena (Redwood SE): i set a soft quota of 12 GPUs equivalent for the pilot to isolate you. autoscale did trigger but the cluster did reshard when another tenant burst so the soft quota behaved conservatively; we can bump or reserve dedicated capacity if you want a hard isolation.

[11:20] Marta (BlueArc): what's the procurement lead time on reserved capacity? we might need it next quarter.

[11:28] Samir (Redwood): reserved capacity lead times vary; after signature we can provision dedicated pools within 2-3 weeks depending on region availability. we'll follow up with pricing and slots.

[11:40] Zack (BlueArc ML): quick question on telemetry: what level of token-level tracing do you collect by default and can we opt-out of collecting payloads?

[11:52] Lena (Redwood SE): default traces include token counts, latency, model id, and anonymized prompts; payload retention is configurable and for PHI customers we recommend disabling raw prompt retention and keeping only hashes and diff-based checksums.

[12:08] Priya (BlueArc Security): please put that guidance in writing in the security pack.

[12:15] Samir (Redwood): will do.

[12:20] Omar (Redwood CSM): i want to call out two operational items: 1) we'll create a staged provisioning window for the creds handoff; 2) we'll set up a short SLA doc for the pilot so both sides have expectations on uptime and incident response.

[12:36] Marta (BlueArc): agreed. also can we add a small acceptance test — like 1k prompts with our gold set and 95% pass threshold on the eval?

[12:48] Lena (Redwood SE): yes that's doable. we'll run the eval and share the results.

[13:00] Devon (BlueArc SRE): on the bench side, can we re-run the tests during your off-peak time to avoid background autoscale noise?

[13:08] Lena (Redwood SE): yes, schedule the run and we'll coordinate to drain noisy tenants.

[13:14] Priya (BlueArc Security): one more: for KMS logs, what TTL do you keep by default? our compliance needs 7 years for certain artifacts.

[13:24] Samir (Redwood): retention is configurable; hosted default is 90 days but we offer long-term retention as an add-on or via S3 export; we'll document options in the follow-up.

[13:38] Marta (BlueArc): ok, good. any risks we should call out now?

[13:44] Lena (Redwood SE): main risk is noisy neighbor reshard during a benchmark — mitigated by soft quota or reserved capacity. security risk is key transfer; we'll use wrapped keys and an ops window. quality risk is model variant mismatch; we'll run evals and canary accordingly.

[14:05] Samir (Redwood): great. last bit: next steps recap. Omar will schedule a 1-hour provisioning window (owner: Omar). samir will send SOC2 excerpt and SSO guide. lena will upload bench harness and eval recipe. devon will validate VPC peering and ports. priya will approve transfer method.

[14:28] Marta (BlueArc): thanks everyone. any other quick items?

[14:34] Zack (BlueArc ML): just curious — do you have an internal runbook we can peek at for rollback?

[14:40] Omar (Redwood CSM): yes, we'll include a short rollback playbook with the pilot success criteria doc.

[14:48] Samir (Redwood): ok wrapping — thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

[15:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms ("KV cash" for KV cache), filler words included, speaker labels sometimes simplified.
